after.title: AWS: Service is operating normally: [RESOLVED] Elevated API issues and Launch Failures (ap-northeast-1)
after.summary:
Between 6:46 AM and 9:46 AM PST, we experienced elevated API error rates and launch failures primarily centered in a single Availability Zone (apne1-az1). We also experienced impact to other services such as ECS and Fargate Task Launch failures, ELB provisioning delays, Nat Gateway failures for Create and Disassociate workflows and Managed Flink application state transitions delays. Running EC2 instances and existing workflows were not affected. During this time, EC2 and EBS health data was missing or delayed for the affected Availability Zone resulting in CloudWatch alarms to transition to INSUFFICENT_DATA state and the DescribeInstanceStatus API to return Insufficient Data.
We had identified the root cause and began our mitigation efforts by 7:47 AM, and by 9:46 AM we were seeing broad recovery for APIs and were able to see new EC2 launches succeed. While monitoring for full recovery, we began to observe that new launches in the single affected Availability Zone were experiencing connectivity issues, instance to instance connectivity was unaffected as was instances launched before the impact began. We were able to identify that this shared a root cause to the initial issue.
We took multiple parallel paths to mitigate the connectivity issue, and saw first signs of recovery for the connectivity issue at 11:51 AM and full recovery by 12:31 PM. The issue has been resolved and the service is operating normally.

Resolved - On October 30, 2026, from 17:50 to 18:32 UTC, Actions, Pages, and Webhooks experienced degraded performance. Actions workflow processing, Pages deployments, and webhook deliveries were delayed, and code search and live updates returned errors. Some Actions queues took additional time to drain after mitigation, and the incident was resolved at 19:23 UTC.
The impact was triggered by maintenance on a cloud network gateway connecting an Actions service in the GitHub data center to Redis clusters in the Central US Azure region. The service's Redis client retried aggressively and redialed those connections. That produced a connection storm that saturated the gateway, with about 90% of connection attempts failing. Other services sharing the same network path were degraded as well.
We mitigated the incident by removing the affected resources from rotation, which ended the connection storm and allowed the gateway to recover. We have already reduced the number of connection retries in the impacted service and are further improving retry behavior with jittered backoff, shorter connect timeouts, and retry budgets. We are also working with our infrastructure team to make GitHub more resilient to gateway maintenance.

During this window, a storage dependency that Actions uses to process workflow logs and artifacts throttled our requests. This slowed result processing, causing updates to queue up. The queue was fully processed by 07:27 UTC, shortly after the throttling stopped.
To reduce the risk of recurrence, we have added several storage accounts to increase capacity, and we are working on additional steps to continue to scale.
